body:
Fixed by construction on `claude/sqlite-datetime-filter-empty-hradlv`, rather than by a sort-side change.

The root cause named here — one column holding both INTEGER-epoch and ISO-TEXT values — no longer occurs: `Field.datetime` now has a single canonical storage form, `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SS.sssZ`, written by `formatInput` on every dialect, with existing rows converged by `backfillCanonicalDatetimes` at schema sync. Fixed-width UTC text means lexicographic order **is** chronological order, so `ORDER BY` is correct reading the raw column — and can use an index, which the expression-sort alternative sketched in this issue would have given up.

The repro from this issue is now a regression test (`sql-driver-datetime-canonical-storage.test.ts`, "sorts chronologically as TEXT — lexicographic order IS time order"). It alternates the write shape (`Date` / ISO string) across rows so a form-sensitive sort would interleave them wrongly, and asserts both `find({orderBy})` and a raw `ORDER BY` produce chronological order.

The "stop producing the mix at all" direction this issue proposed as the durable alternative is what was taken. Full rationale — including why canonical text was chosen over the epoch integer, and the measured Postgres timezone divergence found while checking whether this was SQLite-only — is in the ADR-0053 addendum (D-B1 through D-B3) on that branch.

Leaving this open until the branch merges.
